annotations.text:
WHERE — AIP Review, one office

History sits in the header between the state chip and the decision buttons (dashed outline = new).

It is there at EVERY status, not only when the office is with PPDO. A reviewer opening an accepted or returned office is exactly the person who wants to know how it got there.

WHERE — AIP Entry, own office

Drawn inside the submit panel's header, next to Re-submit (flip the 'stage' chip for the locked 'With PPDO' case — the button stays).

Everyone who can open their own office's AIP Entry sees it — encoders too, not only the department head. The server clamps it to their own office.

RESOLVED 2026-09-14: keep it in the submit panel, as drawn.

RESOLVED 2026-09-14 — comments grouped under hand-offs, as drawn.

Drawn: the chain is hand-offs only, and each hand-off holds the comments written while the office sat in that state — collapsed to a count ('3 comments while with PPDO · 1 still unresolved'), opened on demand. Two are drawn open, the oldest closed.

A flat list interleaving every comment gets long fast on an office with 80 activities, and buries the submit/return chain Ralph asked to backtrack. Recommend grouped.

Flip the 'state' chip for loading, empty and error.

SETTLED BY WHAT EXISTS — no decision needed unless you disagree

• A resolve shows on the comment ('Resolved by … · date'), not as its own line in the chain.
• A comment on a deleted row stays, marked 'Row deleted' (spec §5.1).
• A return carries no reason field — the endpoint takes none; the comments are the reason.
• One line per hand-off, never one per sub-office group.
• Newest first, Manila time. No export or print.
• Comments written before the first submit sit under a 'Before first submission' line at the bottom (not drawn).
